milestone: G7c — oracle bottleneck ladder: can a frozen core consume a LOSSY latent?
why: Every result so far (G1..G6) is built on a 25-dim LOSSLESS, CLOSED S5 schema. Natural-language facts are unbounded, heterogeneous and necessarily lossy. Whether a frozen backbone can consume a lossy representation AT ALL is completely untested and is on the critical path to natural language. This gap is INDEPENDENT of the unresolved composition mechanism (G7a/G7b), so it is not blocked by it.
no_training: Frozen core, frozen zdelta-v1. Nothing is trained. This is an oracle ladder, not a repair. Retraining delivery on lossy latents is a SEPARATE, later question and must not be tuned using these numbers.

degradations_pre_locked.erase: keep r of the 25 coordinates (fixed random subset, fixed seed), zero the rest
degradations_pre_locked.project: fixed random orthonormal basis; keep the top r components, reconstruct
degradations_pre_locked.quant: uniform quantisation of each coordinate to r levels on [0,1]

must_report_per_cell: text ceiling (censor the cell if the text teacher is below 95%)
schema fidelity: does latent_to_perm(degraded) still recover the permutation? This separates 'the latent lost the information' from 'the backbone could not consume it'

reading_rules.consumption_failure: schema fidelity stays 100% but accuracy/dm tail degrades -> the backbone cannot CONSUME a lossy-but-sufficient latent. This is the interesting failure.
reading_rules.information_failure: schema fidelity drops with r -> the information is simply gone; a delivery failure there says nothing about consumption.
reading_rules.for_stage_3: If the same tail appears even at lossless or mild loss, that justifies state separation. If it only breaks under strong compression, fix schema/interface capacity FIRST and do not treat a structural architecture change as a universal remedy.

axes_kept_separate: mixed and allph are reported separately throughout; G7a/G7b established that the allph degradation is a different, still-unexplained axis and must not be merged with mixed.
